newsitem.title: UK: Seal bites woman in British nature reserve.
newsitem.headline: Seal bites woman in British nature reserve.

text.p: An 80-year-old woman was in hospital on Wednesday night after a wild seal lunged at her and bit her leg in a British nature reserve.

The seal -- more than three metres long and weighing 190 kilos -- was trying to protect its pup. A seal has a bite 10 times worse than a Rottweiler and officials said the area was currently as hazardous as an African wildlife park.

"Walking through this reserve at the moment is as dangerous as going through the Serengeti big game park," said Roger Parsons, a spokesman for the Lincolnshire Trust for Nature Conservation where the woman was bitten.
"These are big beasts and although they look charming they are very dangerous indeed," he said.

The woman had been walking along a coastal path near Mablethorpe in eastern England when the seal grabbed hold of her coat and bit her leg. The woman, who has asked not to be identified, was expected to stay in hospital for several days.
